records.source: וּמָרְדֳּכַ֗י יָדַע֙ אֶת־כָּל־אֲשֶׁ֣ר נַעֲשָׂ֔ה וַיִּקְרַ֤ע מָרְדֳּכַי֙ אֶת־בְּגָדָ֔יו וַיִּלְבַּ֥שׁ שַׂ֖ק וָאֵ֑פֶר וַיֵּצֵא֙ בְּת֣וֹךְ הָעִ֔יר וַיִּזְעַ֛ק זְעָקָ֥ה גְדֹלָ֖ה וּמָרָֽה׃
records.gloss: And Mordecai knew all that had been done, and tore Mordecai his clothes and put on sackcloth and ashes, and went out into [the] midst of the city and cried out [with] a cry great and bitter.
pieces: When Mordecai learned all that had been done, he tore his clothes, put on sackcloth and ashes, and went out into the middle of the city, crying out loudly and bitterly.

L.1: And Mordecai knew all that had been done, and Mordecai tore his clothes and put on sackcloth and ashes, and he went out into the middle of the city and cried out with a loud and bitter cry.

R.1: When Mordecai found out everything that had happened, he tore his clothes to show his grief. He dressed in rough sackcloth and put ashes on himself. Then he went out into the city and wailed loudly and bitterly.

decisions.choice: tore his clothes, put on sackcloth and ashes: the signs of deep mourning
decisions.reason: Tearing one's clothes, wearing sackcloth (a coarse cloth of goat hair) and putting ashes or dust on oneself were the customary signs of grief and humbling oneself (Genesis 37:34; 2 Samuel 13:19; Jonah 3:6; Daniel 9:3).

decisions.choice: all that had been done: the whole matter, including what was not made public
decisions.reason: Mordecai knows more than the published decree: he knows the exact sum Haman promised (verse 7). The text does not say how he learned it.

decisions.choice: a loud and bitter cry
decisions.reason: The same words describe Esau's cry when he lost his father's blessing (Genesis 27:34). The cry is a public lament, raised in the middle of the city.

decisions.choice: to show his grief; rough sackcloth
decisions.reason: Readable explains what tearing clothes meant and what sackcloth was, for readers who do not know the customs.

records.heading: Mordecai urges Esther to plead for her people

records.source: וַיָּב֕וֹא עַ֖ד לִפְנֵ֣י שַֽׁעַר־הַמֶּ֑לֶךְ כִּ֣י אֵ֥ין לָב֛וֹא אֶל־שַׁ֥עַר הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ בִּלְב֥וּשׁ שָֽׂק׃
records.gloss: And he came as far as before [the] gate of the king, for there [is] no going into [the] gate of the king in clothing of sackcloth.
pieces: He went only as far as the front of the king's gate, because no one was allowed to enter the king's gate dressed in sackcloth.

L.2: And he came as far as the front of the king's gate, for no one was to enter the king's gate in clothing of sackcloth.

R.2: He went only as far as the entrance of the palace gate, because no one dressed in sackcloth was allowed to go through it.

decisions.choice: no entering the king's gate in sackcloth: mourning was kept out of the king's presence
decisions.reason: This rule is known only from this verse, but it fits a court where nothing unpleasant was to come before the king. Mordecai's place was in the king's gate (2:19; 3:2); in mourning he cannot take it.

decisions.choice: no one was to enter (Literal); no one was allowed to enter (Balanced)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says only "there is no going into"; English needs a subject. The phrase states a rule, not a physical barrier.

records.source: וּבְכָל־מְדִינָ֣ה וּמְדִינָ֗ה מְקוֹם֙ אֲשֶׁ֨ר דְּבַר־הַמֶּ֤לֶךְ וְדָתוֹ֙ מַגִּ֔יעַ אֵ֤בֶל גָּדוֹל֙ לַיְּהוּדִ֔ים וְצ֥וֹם וּבְכִ֖י וּמִסְפֵּ֑ד שַׂ֣ק וָאֵ֔פֶר יֻצַּ֖ע לָֽרַבִּֽים׃
records.gloss: And in every province and province, [the] place where [the] word of the king and his law [was] reaching, mourning great [was] to the Jews, and fasting and weeping and wailing; sackcloth and ashes was spread [as a bed] for the many.
pieces: In every province where the king's command and his law arrived, there was great mourning among the Jews, with fasting, weeping and wailing. Many of them lay in sackcloth and ashes.

L.3: And in every province, wherever the word of the king and his law reached, there was great mourning among the Jews, and fasting and weeping and wailing; sackcloth and ashes were spread out for many.

R.3: In every province where the king's order and law arrived, the Jews mourned deeply. They went without food, and they wept and cried. Many of them lay down on sackcloth and ashes.

decisions.choice: sackcloth and ashes was spread for many: many lay on sackcloth and ashes
decisions.reason: The verb means to spread out as a bed (Isaiah 58:5; Psalm 139:8). Many did not only wear sackcloth but lay down on it, in ashes, as a sign of grief.

decisions.choice: fasting: going without food in grief, without mention of God
decisions.reason: Elsewhere in Scripture fasting goes with turning to God in a time of danger (Joel 2:12-13; Jonah 3:5-9; Ezra 8:21-23). The book of Esther never names God, and it does not mention prayer here; it describes only what the people did.

decisions.choice: in every province and province: in each and every province
decisions.reason: The repeated noun means "each" (as in 3:12, 14). The mourning spreads as far as the decree goes.

decisions.choice: went without food
decisions.reason: Readable says what fasting is, in plain words.

records.source: וַ֠תָּבוֹאינָהנַעֲר֨וֹת אֶסְתֵּ֤ר וְסָרִיסֶ֨יהָ֙ וַיַּגִּ֣ידוּ לָ֔הּ וַתִּתְחַלְחַ֥ל הַמַּלְכָּ֖ה מְאֹ֑ד וַתִּשְׁלַ֨ח בְּגָדִ֜ים לְהַלְבִּ֣ישׁ אֶֽת־מָרְדֳּכַ֗י וּלְהָסִ֥יר שַׂקּ֛וֹ מֵעָלָ֖יו וְלֹ֥א קִבֵּֽל׃
records.gloss: And came [the] maids of Esther and her eunuchs and told her, and writhed the queen exceedingly; and she sent garments to clothe Mordecai and to remove his sackcloth from on him, and not he accepted [them].
pieces: When Esther's maids and her eunuchs came and told her, the queen was deeply distressed. She sent clothes for Mordecai to wear so that he could take off his sackcloth, but he would not accept them.

L.4: And the maids of Esther and her eunuchs came and told her, and the queen writhed exceedingly. And she sent garments to clothe Mordecai and to remove his sackcloth from him, but he did not accept them.

R.4: Esther's servant girls and her palace officials came and told her about Mordecai. The queen was very upset. She sent him clothes to put on in place of his sackcloth, but he would not take them.

decisions.choice: writhed: was in anguish
decisions.reason: The verb is used of writhing in pain or trembling with fear (Psalm 55:5). Esther is shaken by the news of Mordecai's mourning, though she does not yet know its cause (verse 5).

decisions.choice: she sent clothes; he refused them
decisions.reason: Esther may have hoped that Mordecai could then return to his place at the king's gate (verse 2). His refusal shows that his mourning is not for a private grief that clothes could end.

decisions.choice: eunuch(s) (Literal, Balanced); her palace officials (Readable)
decisions.reason: The word can mean a court officer in general, but those who served the queen and the women's quarters were eunuchs (see the decision at 1:10). Literal and Balanced say "eunuch"; Readable says what they did at court.

records.source: וַתִּקְרָא֩ אֶסְתֵּ֨ר לַהֲתָ֜ךְ מִסָּרִיסֵ֤י הַמֶּ֨לֶךְ֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר הֶעֱמִ֣יד לְפָנֶ֔יהָ וַתְּצַוֵּ֖הוּ עַֽל־מָרְדֳּכָ֑י לָדַ֥עַת מַה־זֶּ֖ה וְעַל־מַה־זֶּֽה׃
records.gloss: And called Esther Hathach, one of [the] eunuchs of the king whom he had stationed before her, and commanded him concerning Mordecai, to know what this [was] and why this [was].
pieces: Then Esther called for Hathach, one of the king's eunuchs whom he had assigned to serve her, and she ordered him to go to Mordecai to find out what this was and why it was happening.

L.5: And Esther called Hathach, one of the king's eunuchs whom he had appointed to attend her, and she commanded him concerning Mordecai, to learn what this was and why it was.

R.5: Then Esther called Hathach. He was one of the king's palace officials, and the king had chosen him to serve her. She sent him to Mordecai to find out what was wrong and why.

decisions.choice: whom he had stationed before her: whom the king had appointed to wait on her
decisions.reason: To "stand before" someone is to be in their service (1 Kings 10:8). Hathach was the king's man assigned to the queen, and he becomes her go-between with Mordecai.

decisions.choice: what this was and why this was: the nature of the trouble and its cause
decisions.reason: Esther knows Mordecai is mourning but not why; the two questions ask what has happened and for what reason.

decisions.choice: eunuch(s) (Literal, Balanced); palace officials (Readable)
decisions.reason: The word can mean a court officer in general, but those who served the queen and the women's quarters were eunuchs (see the decision at 1:10). Literal and Balanced say "eunuch"; Readable says what they did at court.

records.source: וַיֵּצֵ֥א הֲתָ֖ךְ אֶֽל־מָרְדֳּכָ֑י אֶל־רְח֣וֹב הָעִ֔יר אֲשֶׁ֖ר לִפְנֵ֥י שַֽׁעַר־הַמֶּֽלֶךְ׃
records.gloss: And went out Hathach to Mordecai, to [the] open square of the city which [was] before [the] gate of the king.
pieces: So Hathach went out to Mordecai in the city square in front of the king's gate.

L.6: And Hathach went out to Mordecai, to the open square of the city that was in front of the king's gate.

R.6: So Hathach went out to Mordecai in the open square of the city, in front of the palace gate.

decisions.choice: the open square of the city: the public place outside the gate
decisions.reason: The square was the open space in a city, often by a gate, where people met and business was done (Nehemiah 8:1). Mordecai stays outside the gate, where mourners were allowed (verse 2).

records.source: וַיַּגֶּד־ל֣וֹ מָרְדֳּכַ֔י אֵ֖ת כָּל־אֲשֶׁ֣ר קָרָ֑הוּ וְאֵ֣ת׀פָּרָשַׁ֣ת הַכֶּ֗סֶף אֲשֶׁ֨ר אָמַ֤ר הָמָן֙ לִ֠שְׁקוֹל עַל־גִּנְזֵ֥י הַמֶּ֛לֶךְ בַּיְּהוּדִ֖יםלְאַבְּדָֽם׃
records.gloss: And told him Mordecai all that had happened to him, and the exact amount of the silver which had said Haman to weigh out to [the] treasuries of the king, for the Jews, to destroy them.
pieces: Mordecai told him everything that had happened to him, including the exact amount of silver Haman had promised to pay into the king's treasuries for the destruction of the Jews.

L.7: And Mordecai told him all that had happened to him, and the exact amount of the silver that Haman had promised to weigh out to the king's treasuries for the Jews, to destroy them.

R.7: Mordecai told him everything that had happened to him. He also told him exactly how much money Haman had promised to pay into the king's treasury in return for destroying the Jews.

decisions.choice: the exact amount: a precise statement of the sum
decisions.reason: The word means an exact account or declaration (10:2). Mordecai knows the very figure Haman offered (3:9), which suggests that the payment was part of the deal (see the decision at 3:11).

decisions.choice: all that had happened to him: his own part in the story
decisions.reason: Mordecai begins with what happened to him: his refusal to bow and Haman's anger (3:2-6). The matter started with him.

decisions.choice: for the destruction of the Jews (Balanced); in return for destroying the Jews (Readable)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew "for the Jews, to destroy them" means the payment was the price of their destruction; Balanced and Readable say so plainly.

records.source: וְאֶת־פַּתְשֶׁ֣גֶן כְּתָֽב־הַ֠דָּת אֲשֶׁר־נִתַּ֨ן בְּשׁוּשָׁ֤ן לְהַשְׁמִידָם֙ נָ֣תַן ל֔וֹ לְהַרְא֥וֹת אֶת־אֶסְתֵּ֖ר וּלְהַגִּ֣יד לָ֑הּ וּלְצַוּ֣וֹת עָלֶ֗יהָ לָב֨וֹא אֶל־הַמֶּ֧לֶךְ לְהִֽתְחַנֶּן־ל֛וֹ וּלְבַקֵּ֥שׁ מִלְּפָנָ֖יו עַל־עַמָּֽהּ׃
records.gloss: And the copy of [the] writing of the law which had been given in Susa to annihilate them he gave to him, to show Esther and to tell her, and to command her to go to the king to seek favor from him and to make request before him for her people.
pieces: He also gave him a copy of the written law issued in Susa for their destruction, to show to Esther and explain to her. He told him to instruct her to go to the king, beg him for mercy, and plead with him for her people.

L.8: And he gave him the copy of the writing of the law that had been given in Susa to annihilate them, to show it to Esther and to tell her, and to command her to go in to the king to seek his favor and to plead before him for her people.

R.8: He also gave Hathach a copy of the law that had been announced in Susa, ordering the Jews to be destroyed. He told him to show it to Esther and explain it to her. He wanted her to go to the king and beg him to have mercy on her people.

decisions.choice: to seek favor: to plead for mercy
decisions.reason: The verb means to ask for grace or mercy, as a person pleads with someone who has power over them (Genesis 42:21; Hosea 12:5). Esther is to plead, not demand.

decisions.choice: her people: what Esther had kept hidden
decisions.reason: Mordecai had told Esther not to make known her people (2:10, 20). Now he asks her to plead for them, which means revealing that she is a Jew.

decisions.choice: to command her: Mordecai still gives Esther orders
decisions.reason: As before (2:10, 20), Mordecai commands and Esther obeys. In verse 17 this is reversed.

decisions.choice: beg him for mercy, and plead with him
alternatives: seek his favor and make request before him
decisions.reason: Balanced puts the two verbs of request in natural English; Literal keeps closer to the Hebrew.

records.source: וַיָּב֖וֹא הֲתָ֑ךְ וַיַּגֵּ֣ד לְאֶסְתֵּ֔ר אֵ֖ת דִּבְרֵ֥י מָרְדֳּכָֽי׃
records.gloss: And came Hathach and told Esther the words of Mordecai.
pieces: Hathach went back and told Esther what Mordecai had said.

L.9: And Hathach came and told Esther the words of Mordecai.

R.9: Hathach went back and told Esther what Mordecai had said.

decisions.choice: the words of Mordecai: the message, given in full in verse 8
decisions.reason: The verse sums up Hathach's report in one line; the reader already knows what he said.

records.gloss: And said Esther to Hathach, and commanded him to Mordecai,
pieces: Then Esther spoke to Hathach and gave him a message for Mordecai,

L.10: And Esther spoke to Hathach and commanded him [to go] to Mordecai,

R.10: Then Esther gave Hathach this message for Mordecai:

decisions.choice: Esther commanded him to Mordecai: she sent Hathach back with an answer
decisions.reason: The sentence runs on into Esther's message in verse 11. "Commanded him to Mordecai" means she gave Hathach orders to carry to Mordecai.

decisions.choice: [to go]
decisions.reason: Literal brackets the verb English needs to make sense of "commanded him to Mordecai".

records.source: כָּל־עַבְדֵ֣י הַמֶּ֡לֶךְ וְעַם־מְדִינ֨וֹת הַמֶּ֜לֶךְ יֽוֹדְעִ֗ים אֲשֶׁ֣ר כָּל־אִ֣ישׁ וְאִשָּׁ֡ה אֲשֶׁ֣ר יָבֽוֹא־אֶל־הַמֶּלֶךְ֩ אֶל־הֶחָצֵ֨ר הַפְּנִימִ֜ית אֲשֶׁ֣ר לֹֽא־יִקָּרֵ֗א אַחַ֤ת דָּתוֹ֙ לְהָמִ֔ית לְ֠בַד מֵאֲשֶׁ֨ר יֽוֹשִׁיט־ל֥וֹ הַמֶּ֛לֶךְ אֶת־שַׁרְבִ֥יט הַזָּהָ֖ב וְחָיָ֑ה וַאֲנִ֗י לֹ֤א נִקְרֵ֨אתי֙לָב֣וֹא אֶל־הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ זֶ֖ה שְׁלוֹשִׁ֥ים יֽוֹם׃
records.gloss: All [the] servants of the king and [the] people of [the] provinces of the king [are] knowing that every man and woman who goes to the king into the court the inner who is not called, one [is] his law, to put [him] to death, apart from [one] to whom holds out the king the scepter of gold, and he will live; and I have not been called to go to the king these thirty days.
pieces: "All the king's officials and the people of the king's provinces know that if any man or woman goes to the king in the inner court without being summoned, there is only one law: that person is to be put to death, unless the king holds out the gold scepter to them and spares their life. And I have not been summoned to come to the king for thirty days now."

L.11: "All the servants of the king and the people of the king's provinces know that any man or woman who goes to the king into the inner court without being called, there is one law for him: to be put to death, except the one to whom the king holds out the golden scepter, so that he may live. And I have not been called to come to the king these thirty days."

R.11: "Everyone who serves the king, and all the people in his provinces, knows this law: if any man or woman goes to the king in the inner courtyard without being called, they must be put to death. The only way they can live is if the king holds out his gold scepter to them. And the king has not called me to come to him for the past thirty days."

decisions.choice: the inner court, uncalled: no one could come before the Persian king without a summons
decisions.reason: Herodotus describes the same custom at the Persian court: no one might enter the king's presence unless sent for (Histories 1.99; 3.118, 140). Esther, though queen, is bound by it.

decisions.choice: the golden scepter held out: the king's sign of pardon and acceptance
decisions.reason: The king's scepter was the sign of his royal power; holding it out to someone who had come uncalled meant he was received and his life spared (5:2; 8:4).

decisions.choice: I have not been called these thirty days
decisions.reason: Esther gives a second reason for fear: the king has not sent for her for a month, so she cannot count on his favor. The text leaves the reason unsaid.

decisions.choice: servants (Literal); officials (Balanced); everyone who serves the king (Readable)
decisions.reason: The king's servants are his court officials; Literal keeps "servants".

decisions.choice: them, their life (Balanced); they, them (Readable)
decisions.reason: The law applies to "any man or woman"; Balanced and Readable use "they" and "them" to refer back to that person, since the Hebrew "his" covers both.

records.gloss: And they told Mordecai the words of Esther.
pieces: When Esther's words were reported to Mordecai,

L.12: And they told Mordecai the words of Esther.

R.12: When Mordecai was told what Esther had said,

decisions.choice: they told: the messengers, not named
decisions.reason: The verb is plural. Hathach may have been one of several who carried messages, or the plural is used without a definite subject, "Mordecai was told". Hathach is not named again in the book.

decisions.choice: When ... (Balanced, Readable), joined to verse 13
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable make this short verse the opening of the next sentence, so it ends with a comma.

records.source: וַיֹּ֥אמֶר מָרְדֳּכַ֖י לְהָשִׁ֣יב אֶל־אֶסְתֵּ֑ר אַל־תְּדַמִּ֣י בְנַפְשֵׁ֔ךְ לְהִמָּלֵ֥ט בֵּית־הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ מִכָּל־הַיְּהוּדִֽים׃
records.gloss: And said Mordecai to send back to Esther, Do not imagine in your soul to escape [in the] house of the king from all the Jews.
pieces: he sent back this answer to Esther: "Do not imagine that because you are in the king's palace you alone of all the Jews will escape.

L.13: And Mordecai said to send back to Esther, "Do not imagine in your soul that you will escape in the king's house, more than all the Jews.

R.13: he sent this answer back to Esther: "Do not think that just because you live in the king's palace, you will be the only Jew who escapes.

decisions.choice: imagine in your soul: think to yourself
decisions.reason: The word often translated "soul" here means the self, the inner person; "to imagine in your soul" is to think privately or suppose.

decisions.choice: escape in the king's house from all the Jews: be the one Jew who escapes because she is in the palace
alternatives: escape from all the Jews by being in the king's house
decisions.reason: The words "from all the Jews" set Esther apart from her people: she should not suppose that the palace will make her the exception. The decree names all the Jews, and the queen is one of them.

decisions.choice: said to send back (Literal); sent back this answer (Balanced)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew "said to return" means that Mordecai gave a message to be carried back. Literal keeps the Hebrew shape.

records.source: כִּ֣י אִם־הַחֲרֵ֣שׁ תַּחֲרִישִׁי֮ בָּעֵ֣ת הַזֹּאת֒ רֶ֣וַח וְהַצָּלָ֞ה יַעֲמ֤וֹד לַיְּהוּדִים֙ מִמָּק֣וֹם אַחֵ֔ר וְאַ֥תְּ וּבֵית־אָבִ֖יךְ תֹּאבֵ֑דוּ וּמִ֣י יוֹדֵ֔עַ אִם־לְעֵ֣ת כָּזֹ֔את הִגַּ֖עַתְּ לַמַּלְכֽוּת׃
records.gloss: For if indeed you keep silent at the time the this, relief and deliverance will arise for the Jews from a place other, and you and [the] house of your father will perish; and who [is] knowing whether for a time like this you have reached the kingdom?
pieces: For if you remain silent at this time, relief and rescue will come to the Jews from another place, but you and your father's family will perish. And who knows? Perhaps you have become queen for a time like this."

L.14: For if you indeed keep silent at this time, relief and deliverance will arise for the Jews from another place, and you and the house of your father will perish. And who knows whether it is for a time like this that you have come to the kingdom?"

R.14: If you say nothing now, help and rescue for the Jews will come from somewhere else, but you and your father's family will die. And who knows? Maybe you became queen for a moment just like this."

decisions.choice: from another place: help from some other source, which the text does not name
alternatives: help from God, whose name the book never says
help from some other person or power
decisions.reason: Mordecai is sure the Jews will be rescued even if Esther does nothing, but he does not say from where. Many readers see here a hint of God's hidden care for his people; later Jewish writers sometimes used "the Place" as a name for God. The book itself never names God, and the words can also mean help from another person or quarter. The translation keeps the phrase open, as the Hebrew does.

decisions.choice: if you indeed keep silent: a strong conditional, "if you keep quite silent"
decisions.reason: The Hebrew repeats the verb for emphasis. Mordecai warns against saying nothing at all at the moment it counts.

decisions.choice: who knows whether: hope without certainty
decisions.reason: The same words "who knows" introduce a hope that God may yet turn and spare in Joel 2:14 and Jonah 3:9; also 2 Samuel 12:22. Mordecai suggests that Esther's rise to the throne may have a purpose, but he does not claim to know it.

decisions.choice: you and your father's house will perish
decisions.reason: Her father's house is her family line. Mordecai does not say how they would perish: whether in the slaughter, by the king, or as a judgment for failing her people. The warning stands without explanation.

decisions.choice: become queen (Balanced); became queen (Readable)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew "reached the kingdom" means reached royal rank; for Esther that is being queen. Literal keeps "the kingdom".

decisions.choice: relief and rescue (Balanced); help and rescue (Readable)
decisions.reason: The first word means breathing space or relief; the second, deliverance. Balanced uses "rescue" as the plainer word.

records.gloss: And said Esther to send back to Mordecai,
pieces: Then Esther sent back this reply to Mordecai,

L.15: And Esther said to send back to Mordecai,

R.15: Then Esther sent this answer back to Mordecai:

decisions.choice: Esther's reply: the last exchange between them in this chapter
decisions.reason: The sentence runs on into Esther's message in verse 16. It is the third message carried between them (verses 10, 13).

records.source: לֵךְ֩ כְּנ֨וֹס אֶת־כָּל־הַיְּהוּדִ֜ים הַֽנִּמְצְאִ֣ים בְּשׁוּשָׁ֗ן וְצ֣וּמוּ עָ֠לַי וְאַל־תֹּאכְל֨וּ וְאַל־תִּשְׁתּ֜וּ שְׁלֹ֤שֶׁת יָמִים֙ לַ֣יְלָה וָי֔וֹם גַּם־אֲנִ֥י וְנַעֲרֹתַ֖י אָצ֣וּם כֵּ֑ן וּבְכֵ֞ן אָב֤וֹא אֶל־הַמֶּ֨לֶךְ֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר לֹֽא־כַדָּ֔ת וְכַאֲשֶׁ֥ר אָבַ֖דְתִּי אָבָֽדְתִּי׃
records.gloss: Go, gather all the Jews who are found in Susa, and fast for me, and do not eat and do not drink three days, night and day; also I and my maids will fast so; and in this [way] I will go to the king, which [is] not according to the law; and as I have perished, I have perished.
pieces: "Go and gather all the Jews who are in Susa, and fast for me. Do not eat or drink for three days, night or day. My maids and I will fast in the same way. Then I will go to the king, even though it is against the law. And if I perish, I perish."

L.16: "Go, gather all the Jews who are found in Susa, and fast on my behalf, and do not eat and do not drink for three days, night and day. I and my maids will also fast in the same way. And so I will go in to the king, which is not according to the law. And if I perish, I perish."

R.16: "Go and gather all the Jews who live in Susa. Fast for me. Do not eat or drink anything for three days, night or day. My servant girls and I will also fast. Then I will go to the king, even though it is against the law. If I die, I die."

decisions.choice: fast for me: go without food on my behalf
decisions.reason: To fast "for" someone is to fast on their behalf, for their sake. In Scripture such fasting goes with seeking God's help (Ezra 8:21-23; Jonah 3:5-9), but as everywhere in this book, God is not named and prayer is not mentioned.

decisions.choice: three days, night and day, with no food or drink: a total fast
decisions.reason: Going without water as well as food for three days is an extreme fast (compare Exodus 34:28; Jonah 3:7). Esther goes to the king "on the third day" (5:1).

decisions.choice: if I perish, I perish: accepting the risk
decisions.reason: The words echo Jacob's resigned "if I am bereaved, I am bereaved" when he sent Benjamin to Egypt (Genesis 43:14). Esther takes up Mordecai's word "perish" (verse 14) and accepts that she may die.

decisions.choice: not according to the law: against the law of verse 11
decisions.reason: Esther knows she is breaking the court law by going in uncalled; she goes anyway.

decisions.choice: If I die, I die
decisions.reason: Readable uses the plainer word for perish; the meaning is the same.

records.gloss: And passed on Mordecai and did according to all that had commanded him Esther.
pieces: So Mordecai went away and did everything Esther had instructed him.

L.17: And Mordecai went away and did according to all that Esther had commanded him.

R.17: So Mordecai left and did everything Esther told him to do.

decisions.choice: went away: passed on, went off to do it
alternatives: crossed over (to another part of the city)
decisions.reason: The verb means to pass along or cross. Here it most likely means that Mordecai left the square to carry out Esther's word.

decisions.choice: did all that Esther had commanded him: the roles are reversed
decisions.reason: Until now Mordecai commanded and Esther obeyed (2:10, 20; 4:8). Now Esther gives the orders and Mordecai carries them out.
